input: Get my bike tuned up at the local shop

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A basic tune-up (brakes, gears) differs greatly from a full overhaul (bearings, cables, full clean); knowing what is needed determines which service package to book and the likely cost.
The timing of when the bike is needed affects how urgently the appointment must be made and whether same-day drop-off is acceptable or advance booking is required.
The user may not yet have a specific shop in mind; knowing whether they need help finding one changes the first action entirely.
A budget cap determines which service tier the user can choose and whether extra repairs flagged by the mechanic should be approved.
If the bike belongs to someone else (e.g. a child or partner) it affects who transports it and who communicates with the shop.
Knowing the primary problem symptoms (squeaky brakes, slipping gears, flat tyres) helps the user communicate clearly with the mechanic and verify the job is done right.
Some users want to stay involved (approve extra repairs, pick up same day), while others prefer to hand it off completely; this shapes how the task is structured.

gold.taskTitle: Get bike tuned up at local shop
gold.taskDescription: Take the user's bike to a local repair shop to have it serviced and tuned up.

questions.title: What specific issues does your bike currently have?
questions.description: Understanding the known problems (e.g. slipping gears, squeaky brakes, flat tyre) helps define what to tell the mechanic and what a successful tune-up looks like.

questions.title: Do you want a basic tune-up or a full service?
questions.description: Clarifies the scope of work — from a simple adjustment of brakes and gears to a comprehensive overhaul including cables, bearings, and deep cleaning.

questions.title: Do you already have a local shop in mind?
questions.description: Determines whether the first action is booking an appointment or first researching and choosing a nearby shop.

questions.title: When do you need the bike ready to use again?
questions.description: The deadline or target date drives the urgency of booking and whether a quick turnaround must be requested from the shop.

questions.title: What is your budget for this service?
questions.description: A spending limit determines which service tier fits and whether to pre-authorise the shop for any additional repairs they may discover.

questions.title: Is this bike yours, or does it belong to someone else?
questions.description: If the bike belongs to a child, partner, or someone else, it affects who is responsible for drop-off, pick-up, and decision-making at the shop.

questions.title: How involved do you want to be during the repair process?
questions.description: Some people want to approve any extra work before it is done; others prefer to be hands-off. This shapes how the task handoff to the shop is structured.
